assays.assay_name: Home-cage behavioural activity scoring (active vs inactive)
assays.assay_description: During EEG sessions, an experienced observer blindly scored the rats' behaviour as active behaviour or inactivity in the home cage in parallel with EEG recording. A 10-min baseline period was recorded before drug administration and 90 min after subcutaneous treatment; behavioural ratios were calculated per 10-min epoch.

application_type.evidence: All of the substances were administered subcutaneously in a dose of 2 ml/kg of animal weight.

setup_habituation.evidence: Approximately 15 mins before the experiment began, the animals were connected to the EEG system in their home cages. A 10-min recording session was obtained immediately before treatment to serve as a baseline condition.

setup_restrain.evidence: The rats were able to move freely in the cage during all of the EEG recording sessions while being connected with a cable to the amplifier.

food_restriction.evidence: Access to standardized food and water was ad libitum.

water_restriction.evidence: Access to standardized food and water was ad libitum.

time_to_assay.evidence: Subsequently, treatments were administered, and registration continued for another 90 min.

sample_size.evidence: 10 rats for saline, nine rats for LSD, eight for psilocin, 12 for mescaline, and 11 for DOB were selected for signal analysis

outcomes.summary: Behavioural activity (ratio of active to inactive time) was not significantly different between psychedelic-treated groups (psilocin, LSD, mescaline, DOB) and saline controls during the 90-min post-treatment recording, although a significant time × treatment interaction was detected.
outcomes.statistics: F(8,86) = 2.29, P < 0.05 (time × treatment interaction); Tukey post hoc: no significant effects between control and active substances at the appropriate times
outcomes.evidence: Despite the significant interaction revealed by repeated-measures ANOVA between time and treatment (F(8,86) = 2.29, P < 0.05), Tukey's post hoc analysis showed no significant effects between the control group and the active substances at the appropriate times.

judge_notes: Paper's primary measurements are EEG (cross-spectral and phase-lagged coherence, power spectra), which are neural recordings excluded by the rubric. The only behavioural readout is the parallel active-vs-inactive scoring used to gate EEG analysis — included as a single behavioural assay (home-cage behavioural activity scoring) following the qwen candidate.
GLM candidate produced no assay entries; qwen's home-cage behavioural scoring entry was retained as the lone behavioural paradigm.
group_housing scored 'no' because rats were individually separated post-surgery up through recording, which is the housing during behavioural testing (qwen's interpretation preferred over glm's).

setup_habituation scored 'yes': animals were connected to the EEG system in their home cages ~15 min before experiment plus a 10-min pre-treatment baseline, constituting apparatus/tethering habituation.
